title: supermarket/employees
description: One row per member of store staff. Shop-floor and management staff, each assigned to one store. Cashiers appear as the operator on till transactions, which is what links this table into the sales data.

store_id.description: The store this person works at. Everybody is assigned to exactly one store in this dataset.

employee_code.description: Payroll reference, the number that appears on a rota and on the bottom of a till receipt.

full_name.description: Spanish name with two surnames -- the father's followed by the mother's -- which is worth testing any name-splitting code against.

national_id.description: Spanish DNI, eight digits plus a check letter computed modulo 23. Structurally valid, so it passes a real DNI validator.

role.description: Job title. Cashiers dominate, as they do in a real shop, and only they appear as transaction operators.

hired_at.description: Start date, always on or after the store's own opening date -- nobody was hired into a shop that did not exist.

hourly_rate.description: Gross pay per hour in euros, from around the Spanish minimum wage for shop-floor roles up to about 25 for a store manager.

active.description: Whether the person still works here. Around 12% have left, which is a realistic retail turnover rate and gives you inactive rows to exclude.
